RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the July 16, 2004/Asadha 25, 1926 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs,
Food and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests; Food Processing
Industries; Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions—20
Production of sugar
†*161. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) the total production of sugar in the
country during 2003-04 and to what extent
this is less in comparison to last year's
production;
(b) whether Government propose to
import sugar keeping in view the less
production of sugar; if not, the reasons
therefor; and
(c) the steps being taken by
Government to increase the production for
striking a balance between consumption of
sugar and the prices?
Expansion of game sanctuaries
*162. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
extend the land area under game sanctuaries
by buying up adjacent land;
(b) whether it is a fact that there is a
Server1\1101RS QLOral EV 16 July\1101RS 49
need to extend the area reserved for game
sanctuaries;
(c) whether any plan is under
consideration of Government to help State
Governments acquire nearby land to
sanctuaries;
(d) if so, the details of such plans; and
(e) the States which have been selected
for this purpose?
Broad gauge line in Lumding-Silchar
sector
*163. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the progress of the
work on broad gauge line between Lumding-
Silchar sector of North-Frontier Railways;
(b) by when this project is expected to
be completed;
(c) whether Government will take
initiative to provide the additional funds
from DONER and other sources to
complete the work;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Status of Sher-e-Kashmir University
*164. SHRI T. S. BAJWA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the present status of proposed Sher-
e-Kashmir University of Agriculture,
Science and Technology in Jammu and
Kashmir;
(b) the total amount sanctioned for the
purpose and the amount utilized so far;
(c) the land acquired for the purpose so
far, and the compensation paid to the land-
owners; and
(d) by when, the whole project is likely
to be completed?
New rail line in Manipur
*165. SHRI RISHANG KEISHING:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) the names of the State capitals in the
country which are not yet connected by
rail;
(b) whether survey of Jiribam-Tupul,
new rail line in Manipur has been
completed; and
(c) if so, the estimated cost of the
project, the likely time to start and to
complete the rail project?
Environment clearance for urban
projects
*166. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have issued a
notification making it mandatory for urban
projects to get environment clearance;
(b) whether the new projects relating to
construction of new townships and
settlement colonies, commercial complexes
etc. have also come under the purview of
Environment Impact Assessment;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government are aware that
several new townships are being developed
around Butkal Lake and Surajkund Lakes,
Haryana;
(e) if so, whether the promoters have
taken environment clearance; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Telephonic railway enquiry service
†*167. SHRIMATI SAVITA
SHARDA: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number
of people call upon railway enquiry
telephonically to get trains related
information and they generally complain
about no response;
(b) if so, whether Government have
formulated any new plan to improve the
railway enquiry service on telephone; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Cost of AIDS and Cancer drugs
*168. SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the fact that the life saving
medicines for treatment of HIV/AIDS and
Cancer are not under price control;
(b) if so, whether Government have
conducted any survey to ascertain the cost

MoU between IGKV and Swiss MNC
   493. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Raipur based Indira
Gandhi Krishi Viswavidyalaya, having a
collection of rice germplasm of 22972
varieties, proposes to sign a Memorandum
of Understanding with “Syngenta”, the
Swiss multinational corporation, to take
over all the paddy varieties in the custody
of the universities;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether farmers and agricultural
workers have represented against the MoU
and requested to assert their rights over the
variety of paddy seeds; and
(d) if so, the action taken thereon?
Reducing the agro-import for
prosperity of rural economy
  †494. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether, addressing a peasants’ rally
in Maharashtra he said that the Central
Government would make an effort to reduce
agro-import for the prosperity of local rural
economy and Government are considering
to provide 40 per cent of subsidy for
promoting horticulture and extending the
repaying period of loan given to the
sugarcane growers; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Legislation on cow slaughter
   †495. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to refer to answer to Unstarred
Question 585, given in the Rajya Sabha on
the 25th July, 2003 and state:
(a) by when the Central legislation
which is being contemplated to be enacted
by Government to ban the cow slaughter,
keeping in view the deep respect and
feelings of the people of this country
towards cow, would be introduced; and
(b) the reason for delay in introducing
the same?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Foodgrains production
   496. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the rate of growth in the
production of foodgrains is progressing
continuously during the last three years; if
so, the details thereof;
(b) the status of production of foodgrains
during the last three years, State-wise;
(c) what steps Government are
contemplating to take in order to give
enough remunerative prices for the
foodgrains during procurements; and
(d) whether the entry of the foodgrains
and other essential commodities into the
country from abroad will be controlled to
safeguard the interest of the growers?
Production and export of mangoes
   †497. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the total production of mangoes in
the  country during this year, State-wise;
(b) the steps taken/being taken by
Government to increase the production of
mangoes in the country; and
(c) the State-wise quantity of mangoes
exported alongwith names of the countries
to which exported togetherwith the value
of mangoes exported and the target laid
down for future?
Linking each district with KVKs
   †498.   SHRI RISHANG KEISHING:
             SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
recently to link each district of the country
with Krishi Vigyan Kendra;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the number of districts particularly
of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and
North-Eastern Region till date where Krishi
Vigyan Kendras are set up and the number
of districts not having Krishi Vigyan
Kendras; and
(d) by when every district in the
country can have a Krishi Vigyan Kendra?
Manufacturing of life-saving drugs
   499. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
pharmaceutical companies are requesting
for inclusion of a provision to protect them
in the third Patent Amendment Bill so that
the companies manufacturing life-saving
drugs need not withdraw hundreds of
brands amounting to nearly Rs. 4000 crores
after the Product Patent Act comes into
effect from 2005;
(b) if so, the details of drugs which face
threat of withdrawal; and
(c) the measures Government are taking
or propose to take to protect the domestic
life-saving drug manufacturers?
Availability of milk at affordable price
  500. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the approximate milk production
alongwith its growth rate in the country,
State-wise; and
(b) the measures taken to increase the
production and to achieve the target of milk
at affordable price for all the children?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
